Theorem
[Morse connectivity of sublevel sets]

Source: petersen:page-0277 ↗ def:pet-ch6-l-connected ↗ def:pet-ch6-critical-point-index 1. ch6:6.5.2Let $f:M\to \mathbb {R}$ be smooth and proper. If $b$ is not a critical value and every critical point in $f^{-1}([a,b])$ has index $\ge m$, then $f^{-1}((-\infty ,a))\subset f^{-1}((-\infty ,b))$ is $(m-1)$-connected.
Proof

\sketch The Morse deformation removes critical points of index below $m$: avoid each $m$-dimensional negative disk by transversality and push radially out. Every relative sphere of dimension $<m$ therefore deforms below level $a$, proving $(m-1)$-connectivity.

□
